5.2.2 // SELECT & INSTALL A NETWORK ADAPTER

TRAINING MODE

Executive Office — Work Order

You are upgrading a Windows workstation for a corporate networking project. Select the fastest compatible network adapter, install it safely, connect the workstation to the LAN, and verify connectivity.

Required checks

Local server: 192.168.0.10

ISP: 198.28.2.254

Practical checklist

Why the lab matters

Installing a NIC involves PCIe slot compatibility, electrical safety, RJ-45 versus fiber connectors, switch capabilities, and testing with Windows tools.

Hardware hints

For this training scenario the network drop and switch support 10GBASE-T RJ-45. Use a 10 Gb/s PCIe NIC and a Cat6a patch cable. PCIe x8 cards can generally operate in an electrically compatible PCIe x16 slot.

Hardware Workbench
Power ON
Power off the computer, disconnect its power, and open the case. Then select a NIC in the inventory and click the highlighted PCIe expansion slot on the motherboard.

Rear-panel cabling workbench

Choose the cable from Inventory → Cables and connect the workstation's newly installed NIC to the corporate LAN switch.
